newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berliner has bad debt problem - sources.
newsitem.headline: Berliner has bad debt problem - sources.

text.p: Germany's Berliner Bank AG, a subsidiary of Bankgesellschaft Berlin, has bad loans of around one billion marks, banking sources said on Friday.
The bank had no immediate comment on the rumours but said it planned to make an announcement after 1630 GMT.
The sources also said that Wolfgang Steinriede, one of the parent bank's two chief excutives, planned to leave the bank immediately. He would be replaced by Wolfgang Rupf.
Rumours that Bankgesellschaft Berlin was facing serious problems had circulated in financial markets on Friday, pushing the parent bank's shares sharply lower.
A German newspaper reported on Friday that the bank could face losses of up to a billion marks following the collapse of a number of companies owing it money.

Commenting on the decision to make the debt provisions, Bankgesellschaft said, "This is to take account of the continued difficult economic situation in Germany, particularly ...the risk position in east Germany and Berlin."
It added that the decision to make the provisions was in line with the bank's conservative credit policy.

"Against this background and on the basis of the group's solid structure the management board is convinced that the group will register notably better orders for 1997 and the following years," it added.
Moser and Steinriede had tendered their resignations "in the interests of continuity of the bank's development and in pursuit of continued clear leadership responsibility at the bank," it said.
The supervisory board had accepted the resignations, he added.
